source_text.body:
Triage unread email hourly and send Monday briefings
The writer says Muse scans unread email hourly, ranks it by importance, and sends Monday briefings; an early mistake archiving a promo was corrected.
·
Oct 19, 2026
Done with
MM
Meta Muse
What they did
The writer gave Muse access to their email and set it to check unread messages once an hour. Each run, it sent back a numbered list ranked by importance, and the person decided what to do with every item; after Muse once archived a promo email on its own, they corrected it and it stopped touching email without approval. On Mondays, Muse also sent two scheduled briefings: one digesting the AI newsletters they subscribe to and one summarizing updates from fourteen indie builders they follow, with sources attached.
How it went
The system became useful enough that the writer says they cancelled most of those newsletter subscriptions because the Monday briefing replaced them. The main limitation described is trust: after one mistaken auto-archive, they kept humans in the loop for every email action.
Worth knowing
The post says new users got 1 billion free tokens plus a weekly free allowance, which the writer says is enough to run for a long time.
Try it yourself
with
Meta Muse
Copy prompt
Every hour, scan my unread email and rank it by importance: needs a reply today, needs a reply this week, and can wait. Every Monday at [time], send me a briefing with the top items, upcoming deadlines, and anything waiting on someone else. Do not archive or delete anything without asking me first; instead list what you would archive and let me approve it.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/MetaAI/comments/1x8wgb8/two_months_with_metas_muse_the_assistant_that
